title: Jira Pricing in 2026: Free Plan, Paid Tiers and Your Bill
summary: Jira pricing has multiple tiers with additional costs that aren't always obvious, so you can understand the real expense of each plan.
body_markdown:
## Connect Jira to other tools with Activepieces


If the gap is a missing connection rather than a high price, Activepieces sits beside Jira and moves issues to and from other apps outside Jira's own automation quota.


The run is its meter, not the steps inside it: a flow is 1 credit whether it has two steps or ten, so splitting a job into smaller, more reliable steps never raises the bill.


Zapier's per-task billing and Make's per-module billing both charge more as a flow gets finer-grained, which taxes the builder for doing it properly.


It doesn't replace Jira or lower what you pay for it. It covers the work Jira's own automation doesn't reach.


### When Jira's built-in automation is enough


When the whole job happens inside Atlassian, stay with Jira's own automation. That covers assigning an issue, moving it to a new status when a linked one closes, or commenting when a field changes. Those rules cost you nothing extra to set up.


There is a catch: each plan caps how many times rules can run in a month, and the rules mostly act on Atlassian products.


So if your rules are modest and stay inside Jira, adding another tool only gives you one more thing to maintain. Check the run limit for your plan on the pricing page before deciding, because a busy team can hit it sooner than expected.


### Building a Jira to Slack workflow


Once the job leaves Atlassian, Activepieces is where I'd build it, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties already run it.


That means posting to Slack, writing a row in Google Sheets or updating a customer record in a CRM (the system your sales or support team keeps customer details in).


There are 450 integrations in the connectors library, sorted by popularity, and the first screen already shows the plain building blocks: Webhook, Google Sheets, Gmail and HTTP.


That breadth means the tool you need is probably already there, so you're not paying someone to wire it by hand.


1. Set the trigger to a new or updated Jira issue.
2. Add a condition so only the issues you care about continue, such as high priority ones.
3. Send a Slack message with the issue key, title and a link.


Step 2 matters for cost. Every run uses up part of your monthly allowance, so filtering early keeps noise out of the channel and keeps the allowance from draining.


The allowance is the figure to plan around.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) '[pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) shows the free plan at 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows; a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, and if credits run out, flows stay on and runs wait until they refresh.


For testing a flow and running a small team's alerts, the free plan is enough, but a busy project can use it up in days, and then the flows may stop or you pay, depending on the plan.


Activepieces' paid entry plan, Plus, includes 10,000 credits a month, so a team sending a few hundred notifications a week has room to grow.


Zapier, a comparable tool, sets its entry allowances differently, so compare them against your own issue volume, not the headline price.
